death.note: The day line closes «(1563)», which is the whole of what the source gives; no year of birth anywhere.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 30 декабря ст. ст. — «Свт. Макария , митр. Московского (1563).»

attestations.note: The day’s third entry. THE NUMERAL AND THE YEAR ARE LOAD-BEARING: the corpus already keeps `macarius-metropolitan-of-moscow`, display name «Macarius of Moscow (16 February)», who is Macarius (Nevsky, Parvitsky) of 1926 and keeps 16 февраля ст. ст. — a DIFFERENT man, three and a half centuries later, and the reason this folder is an arrival and not an upgrade. The line says «митр. Московского» and the name page «митрополит Московский и всея Руси», which agree, so `metropolitan` and the office `Metropolitan of Moscow` are the source’s own words; the pack carries no «Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus’» and nothing was minted. NO `ru` NAME FORM WAS STORED, and this is a deliberate refusal: the name page is «Святитель Макарий, митрополит Московский и всея Руси», which is a rank word and a rank phrase around a bare forename, and the bare «Макарий» already folds onto three corpus folders under a key `corpus-gate.mjs` prints UNREAD — widening that fold for a form carrying no epithet would buy nothing. The day line’s genitive «Макария ... Московского» was NOT turned into a nominative, a reconstruction this wave refuses. THE READING life6711 WAS OPENED. TWO HYMNS TAKEN, both proper: the kontakion names his own work in so many words — «книжным списанием», the copying of books, and the glorifying of the saints of this land.
